questions.question:
Identify the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required, select No substitution.

By next week I**__ will have been made __**all the reservations for the trip to Europe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. will have made.**

 
• The given sentence is in the **future perfect tense.**
 
• And in the future perfect tense** 'will + have + v3'** is used.
 
• Hence, will have made is the correct answer here.
 
• So, the sentence after substitution will be: **By next week I will have made all the reservations for the trip to Europe.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.**

The lawyer said to the accused, "Where were you at the time of the burglary?"

options.text: The lawyer asked the accused where were you at the time of burglary.
The lawyer asked the accused if he was there at the time of burglary.
The lawyer asked the accused where he had been at the time of the burglary.
The lawyer asked the accused that where was he at the time of burglary.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3.**
 
• When changing a direct sentence to its indirect form, the interrogative sentence becomes an assertive sentence. 'said to' changes to 'asked', second person 'you' changes to the third person 'he', 'were' changes to 'had been'. The remaining part of the sentence remains the same as per the given sentence.
 
• In option 2, the sentence contains an extra adverb 'there' which is not given in the above sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct structure is followed only in option 3 'The lawyer asked the burglar where he was at the time of burglary.'

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate passive form of the given sentence.**

Have you paid your outstanding bills?

options.text: Are your outstanding bills being paid?
Will your outstanding bills be paid?
Have your outstanding bills been paid?
Have your outstanding bills being paid?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3 i.e. Have your outstanding bills been paid?**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2fe49e8c8400270c1bed3d9fe783ce42bf59fb9f7573224dbe504f81e8168661.png] Explanation:**__

 
• While changing the voice the subject and the object exchange their places.
 
 
• 'Your outstanding bills' becomes the subject.
 
 
 
• When changing an active sentence to its passive form, if the sentence is in the present perfect tense, its passive form follows the structure 'has/have + been + V3'. 
 
• In Interrogative sentences, 'auxiliary verb' comes before the subject.
 
• Therefore, the structure is correctly followed by option 3 'Have your outstanding bills been paid?'.

questions.question:
Identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The ambulance have arrived on time, the accident victim was taken to the hospital.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. have arrived on time.**

 
• In the given sentence the use of auxiliary verb **'have' **is wrong.
 
• The given sentence talks about an incident that took place in past so the whole sentence will be in simple past tense.
 
• We need to use past indefinite tense in the first part of sentence so second form of the main verb should be used.
 
• So, the correct sentence will be:** The ambulance arrived on time, the accident victim was taken to the hospital.**

questions.question:
Identify the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required, select No substitution.

Of Rama and Usha __the later is the most__ responsible.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. the latter is the more.**

 
• The word **later **means at a **time in the near future** which does not fit in the context of the given sentence, hence, it will be replaced.
 
• The correct word to be used in the given sentence is **'latter'** which means **second mentioned of two people or things. **
 
• And for making a **comparison** between two things or two persons '**more**' is used.
 
• So, the sentence after improvement will be: **Of Rama and Usha the latter is more responsible. **
